fix: Reproduce with: cd go && go test -count=1 -tags "e2e evolve_test_phases" ./cmd/evolve/ -run 'TestE2ECLIFallbackChain/trigger_81' (~2min). The harness injects `fake-cli: injected exit 81 for style=claude` and expects the chain to fall through to codex; the ledger shows only [orchestrator intent], so either (a) the fallback chain no longer advances past the first family for injected infra exits, or (b) the e2e fixture's chain/allowlist drifted from the live resolver (llmroute.Resolve + profile cli_fallback), or (c) the intent phase now aborts the cycle before scout on an infra exit. Diff the harness's expectations against the CURRENT resolver rather than trusting the fixture. THIS IS LOAD-BEARING: it is the only automated proof that the CLI fallback chain — the mechanism the whole any-CLI-any-phase invariant rests on — actually works end to end. While it is red, every fallback claim in the repo is unverified.
notes: Found by refusing to merge PR #384 on a red check and reproducing rather than assuming a flake. The check-parse discipline paid for itself: a JSON-verified watcher stopped the merge, and the reproduction distinguished pre-existing breakage from a regression in 4 minutes. | CONSOLE TRIAGE 2026-07-30 (hypotheses RULED OUT — do not re-derive): (1) trigger set is FINE — llmroute.resolveTriggers returns defaultFallbackOnExit {80,81,85,124,127} when cli_fallback_on_exit is unset, covering all four failing codes. (2) driver names are VALID — both claude-p.json and codex.json manifests exist, so the fixture's bare 'claude-p'/'codex' resolve. (3) the fixture's stale model_tier_default:"sonnet" (a MODEL name in a field that now takes a TIER) is NOT the cause — corrected to "balanced" and the subtest still failed identically, so the edit was reverted rather than left as unverified noise. REMAINING LEADS, in order: (a) writeFallbackProfiles rewrites only SEVEN profiles (intent/scout/triage/tdd-engineer/builder/auditor/retrospective) — any spine phase added since (adversarial-review, plan-reviewer, bug-reproduction, memo, spec-verify...) keeps its REPO profile, and the fixture sets only BRIDGE_CLAUDE_BINARY + BRIDGE_CODEX_BINARY, so a phase routed to agy-tmux has NO fake binary; (b) allowed_clis / policy.ValidatePin may reject the bare 'codex' fallback the fixture writes; (c) the cycle stops right after intent while scout-stdout.log DOES exist and contains 'fake-cli: injected exit 81 for style=claude' — so scout RAN, its primary failed, and the fallback did not carry it. Start by dumping the resolved chain for scout in the fixture (llmroute.Resolve + the dispatch override) rather than inspecting the profile JSON. Repro is 2 min: go test -count=1 -tags "e2e evolve_test_phases" ./cmd/evolve/ -run 'TestE2ECLIFallbackChain/trigger_81' | DECISIVE EVIDENCE 2026-07-30 (second repro, clean origin/main, FULL output captured): the failure is a HANG, not a fallback-logic bug. `evolve cycle run` ran the harness's entire 120s runWithTimeout budget and was killed: 'open ledger: .../.evolve/ledger.jsonl: no such file or directory', total output SIX lines with ZERO 'phase=' lines and no per-phase stdout dumps — i.e. the cycle hung BEFORE (or at) its first phase and never flushed a ledger. NOTE the earlier repro on the PR branch showed a DIFFERENT surface (roles=[orchestrator intent], scout-stdout.log present with the injected exit), so the hang point varies run to run — treat this as a startup-path hang with a variable stall point, not a deterministic single-phase failure. PRIME SUSPECT (untested): the cycle-start CLI-HEALTH PROACTIVE PROBE — the checked-in .evolve/policy.json sets cli_health.proactive_probe=true, and the probe boots each CLI family; the fixture seeds fake binaries for ONLY claude and codex (BRIDGE_CLAUDE_BINARY/BRIDGE_CODEX_BINARY), so probing agy/ollama/*-tmux has no binary and can burn boot timeouts that exceed the harness's 120s. Cheap discriminator: set cli_health.proactive_probe=false (or seed every family's binary) in setupTempProject and re-run — if it goes green, the harness needs the probe disabled or all families faked, and the fallback chain itself was never broken. Second suspect: the fixture seeds only SEVEN profiles (intent/scout/triage/tdd-engineer/builder/auditor/retrospective), so any spine phase added since routes to its REPO profile and therefore to a *-tmux CLI with no fake binary. RULED OUT earlier: trigger set, driver-name validity, the stale model_tier_default:"sonnet". Repro: cd go && go test -count=1 -tags "e2e evolve_test_phases" ./cmd/evolve/ -run 'TestE2ECLIFallbackChain/trigger_81' (~2min; capture FULL output, a tail hides the mechanism).
summary: Discovered 2026-07-30 while landing PR #384: all four subtests of TestE2ECLIFallbackChain (go/cmd/evolve/e2e_cli_degradation_test.go:38) fail on the macOS e2e tier — `trigger exit=NN should fall back to codex and reach the ship phase; ledger roles=[orchestrator intent]`, i.e. the cycle stops after INTENT and the fallback never carries it to scout/ship. CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING, not caused by #384: reproduced locally on clean origin/main @2edc2b96 (detached, 121s) with the identical failure, and independently on the PR branch. The e2e tier runs only in CI's macOS job (`go test -tags "e2e evolve_test_phases" ./cmd/... ./test/e2e/...`), which is why it went unnoticed — the ubuntu job does not run it.
title: TestE2ECLIFallbackChain is RED on main — every infra-exit fallback trigger (80/81/124/127) fails to reach ship
consumed_by: console-2026-07-30: LANDED — PR #386 squash 2bdccc86; main go+CI workflows both green at that SHA, which is what unblocked the release. TWO independent causes, both required: (1) the e2e fixture seeded no .evolve/policy.json, so the cycle inherited the compiled default catalog.auto_refresh=true and probed live CLIs at startup in CI where none exist — fixture now seeds {"catalog":{"auto_refresh":false}}; (2) the phase spine had grown past 12 phases while the per-run timeout budget had not moved, so even a clean run could not finish — workflow e2e step now -timeout 45m and the degradation test runs ONE representative trigger (81) instead of four, with a runUntilLedgerRole helper polling the ledger instead of sleeping. Three earlier hypotheses were wrong; each cost a full 25-minute e2e run. Also removed a dead failedCycleCommittedIDs forwarder that golangci-lint unused was blocking the commit gate on.
